content.intro: In this lesson, you will study model Error Analysis within Model Evaluation, Validation, and Reliability. You will connect the syllabus topics below to a small, inspectable example and practice stating what the evidence does—and does not—support.
content.why_it_matters: Evaluation is part of system design, not an afterthought. A metric is useful only when it reflects the goal, data conditions, and error costs.

content_blocks.title: The central idea
content_blocks.text: Error analysis examines incorrect predictions to find recurring patterns, missing data, ambiguous labels, or product-level causes. Prioritize fixes by impact and verify whether a change improves the intended outcome without harming other groups.

content_blocks.title: Guided walkthrough
content_blocks.text: 1. Identify what model error analysis takes as input and what result or decision it is intended to support. 2. Read the example before running it and predict the output. 3. Run the small example, compare actual and expected output, then change one input or assumption and repeat. 4. Record what the example demonstrates and what it does not demonstrate about a real system.

content_blocks.title: A practical way to reason about it
content_blocks.text: Start with the task definition and the inputs available. Make the expected behavior explicit, choose a simple reference point, and inspect both ordinary examples and cases where assumptions may fail. content_blocks.text: If the output differs, check indentation and spelling, confirm you saved the intended file, and compare each input value with the example.
